They are complementary written-conventions competencies applied to the same medium (sentence-level writing), giving substantive conceptual coherence, but neither statement's bounded evidence shows that proficiency in sentence structure supports capitalisation or vice versa, and equal grade rank supplies no developmental direction. Shared strand/grade ancestry, the weak 'b2/5' code-prefix overlap and the generic token overlap ('in', 'writing') are nomination signals only, so symmetric relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. Source evidence for both SFIs is truncated (24 omitted items each) and no Learning Components were supplied, limiting finer-grained analysis.
